dirtab.body_radii.title: Body radii used for the discs
dirtab.body_radii.definition: Radius that defines the apparent disc of each body: angular radius = asin(radius / distance).
dirtab.body_radii.algorithm: Read from the planetary constants kernel: Sun radius; Earth equatorial radius (the largest half-width of its slightly flattened disc).

evidence: Angular diameters agree with JPL Horizons to 0.001 arcsec (validation/horizons/results/validation_table.md).

limits: The flattening of the Earth's disc (0.3 %) is not modelled.
No limb darkening, no atmosphere of the Earth.

dirtab.interpolation.title: Interpolation error of the table
dirtab.interpolation.definition: Largest difference between positions interpolated from the table and positions computed directly, in km and as an angle seen from the centre of the Moon.
dirtab.interpolation.algorithm: Recommended interpolation 'lagrange-4-point': for a time between records i and i+1, with u = (t - t_i) / step, each vector component is w(-1) p[i-1] + w(0) p[i] + w(1) p[i+1] + w(2) p[i+2], where w(-1) = -u(u-1)(u-2)/6, w(0) = (u+1)(u-1)(u-2)/2, w(1) = -(u+1)u(u-2)/2, w(2) = (u+1)u(u-1)/6; at the two ends of the table the nearest complete stencil is used. The error is measured at 4000 pseudo-random epochs inside the table against direct SPICE.
dirtab.interpolation.frame: MOON_ME_DE440_ME421: lunar mean-Earth/polar-axis frame, DE440 orientation aligned with the DE421 mean-Earth frame (the frame of the LOLA elevation products)
limits: Valid inside the table only. Interpolate vectors, never angles.

dirtab.positions.title: Apparent positions of the Sun and the Earth
dirtab.positions.definition: Position of the centre of each body relative to the centre of the Moon, in the Moon body-fixed frame, as seen at the record time: corrected for one-way light time and stellar aberration (reception).
dirtab.positions.algorithm: SPICE spkpos(target, et, 'MOON_ME_DE440_ME421', 'LT+S', 'MOON') at every record. A site direction is obtained by subtracting the site position vector and projecting on East, North, Up.
dirtab.positions.frame: MOON_ME_DE440_ME421: lunar mean-Earth/polar-axis frame, DE440 orientation aligned with the DE421 mean-Earth frame (the frame of the LOLA elevation products)

evidence: Test validation/tests/test_horizons.py (comparison with JPL Horizons, thresholds fixed beforehand in validation/horizons/thresholds.json).

28 Horizons cases, 95676 rows: largest direction difference 0.099 arcsec through this table, 0.005 arcsec with the observer at the site (threshold 1 arcsec). Report: validation/horizons/results/validation_table.md.

limits: Light time and stellar aberration are evaluated for the centre of the Moon, not for the site: up to 0.1 arcsec for the Earth, 0.005 arcsec for the Sun.
No terrain and no light bending; directions only.
UTC labels after the last announced leap second assume that no further leap second is introduced.
